veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb (Sy het ... geteken / niemand het gevra) take a comma before en.
In the subordinate (reported) clause the verb belongs at the end; 'groot genoeg vir 'n naam wees' is the natural Afrikaans order.
AWS 2017: two full clauses (Niemand het opgekyk nie / die skêr het aangehou) take a comma before en.
With a bare infinitive, aanhou behaves like begin and bly and takes no ge- in the perfect: 'het aanhou knip'.

veranderings.voor: mooi en spits en so groot
veranderings.rede: A list of three predicates reads more smoothly with a comma than with a repeated en.
'klaar' is awkward as an attributive adjective before a noun; as an adverb after the noun ('twaalf blare klaar') it is natural Afrikaans with the same words.
AWS 2017: two full clauses (Hy het ... probeer skryf / die naam het ... geword) take a comma before en.

veranderings.voor: Mieke se blare en die naam
veranderings.na: Mieke se blare, en die naam
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: two full clauses (Die blaar was groter / die naam het gepas) take a comma before en.
AWS 2017: two full clauses (Die name was groot / almal kon hulle lees) take a comma before en.
AWS 2017: two full clauses (Nandi het dit uitgeknip / die rand loop skeef) take a comma before en.
'deur die klas gedra' reads as carrying something straight through the room; 'rondgedra' says he took the strips round to the children, which the next sentence implies.

vlae.teks: Nandi het nie geantwoord nie en het die potlood by Sipho geleen.
vlae.rede: 'die potlood' points back to the only pencil named so far, which was Thabo's ('Sy potlood' in the previous paragraph), yet she borrows it from Sipho. Either 'n potlood or a different lender would fix it, but which is meant is a content choice for the writer.

vlae.teks: Nandi het dit self uitgeknip en die rand loop effens skeef.
vlae.rede: The story is told in the past tense and this last clause switches to the present ('loop'). That may be deliberate (the leaf still hangs there), so not changed; if not deliberate, 'het die rand effens skeef geloop' would keep the tense.
